missionPremise: The zoningSource mirror (zoningSourceMirror/attachVerdictLayersToFacets, added by CTX-LEAVES PR #644, 301bb75a) projects two of the three earned zoningDistrict rail states (not-applicable, value) onto the served payload but drops the third (refused), letting it fall through to a raw stamp-missing verdict that BP-CONTENT-01 correctly refuses. Measured live on canary cortex-api-00753-feg against the Caldwell jurisdiction cohort: 10 of 25 parcels failed on exactly this.
completionPredicate: A parcel_record zoningDistrict cell of kind=refused produces a served facets.zoning AND provenance.zoningSource that classifyRequiredLeaf (the real hauska-factory verify-walk.mjs grader) grades {state:"refused", ok:true}, carrying the rail's own real reason rather than a fabricated or generic one, without touching the factory grader, REQUIRED_TIER1_FACET_PATHS, any threshold, or mapping refused to any other state. Verified true for all 549 real Caldwell refused zoningDistrict cells (a superset of the 25-parcel/9-jurisdiction cohort, including all three of the dispatch's own named parcels) against the real read-only store, without a deploy.
scopeBasis: Narrowed at CP1 from 'all ZoningFactRefusal codes' to exactly code=="parcel-record-engine-refused" (the rail's own deliberate refusal) after reading the EXISTING test file before writing any fix: two already-passing tests encode a deliberate standing behavior for the other refusal codes -- 'a REFUSED ledger fact is never surfaced -- falls through to the baked stamp' (code parcel-record-malformed-cell) and the ELGIN test ('an unaccounted rail plus an in-city containment gives stamp-missing on BOTH, and absent-verified on NEITHER', code parcel-record-unaccounted, its own comment naming this a 'standing ruling'). Widening the fix to all refusal codes would have silently reversed those deliberate decisions rather than fixing the one gap this dispatch named. Live data confirms this boundary costs nothing for the measured population: all 549 real Caldwell refused zoningDistrict cells are code=parcel-record-engine-refused, zero are any other code.

unitViolationResults.note: classifyRequiredLeaf's own "refused" branch does NOT require a basis/reason (unconditional {state:"refused",ok:true} for any object declaring that state) -- confirmed by reading the grader directly. The dispatch's instruction to carry the reason through is therefore a house-honesty requirement ('every absence carries its basis') stricter than this specific grader instance, not something needed to pass it. Documented explicitly in a test rather than silently assumed.

leave_behind.secondDefectFound: parcelRecordCellRead.ts's interpretParcelRecordCell read a field named `refusal` on a refused cell_state, but the engine has never written that key anywhere in the live store (confirmed: 0 of 549 Caldwell refused zoningDistrict rows, and 0 of the whole store's refused-kind rows sampled, carry `refusal`; all carry `reason`). This was found by tracing 'carry the rail's own reason through' to source rather than trusting the dispatch's own quoted reason text at face value -- the live text differs slightly from the dispatch's quote (the real store has an extra clause: '... -- a data-acquisition gap, not a join failure'), which is what prompted checking the raw field. Fixed in the same PR since it sits directly on this dispatch's own critical path and, unfixed, would have made the entire honest-refusal projection carry a useless generic placeholder for every one of the 549 parcels.

fleetMemoryScratch: LESSON: attachVerdictLayersToFacets's ZoningFactRead union bundles 6 distinct refusal codes under one state:"refused" bucket (engine-refused, unaccounted, invalid-parcel-node-id, cell-miss, malformed-cell, store-not-configured) -- reading the EXISTING test file before writing a fix for 'the refused state' caught that two of those codes already have deliberate, tested, DIFFERENT intended behavior (fall through to city-limits fallback). A dispatch naming 'refused' as one state can mean one specific code within a much wider union; check for existing tests encoding sub-case behavior before broadening a fix to the whole union.

LESSON: a live DB field-name check (interpretParcelRecordCell reads rec.refusal, the engine writes rec.reason) caught a second, independent, silently-broken mechanism that would have made this PR's stated purpose (carry the rail's real reason through) a no-op in practice despite passing every test and the grader -- because the ONE existing test for this code path used a fixture with the SAME wrong key name as the bug, so it could never fail for the right reason. Verifying a 'the reason is real and specific' claim against the actual database, not just the adapter's TypeScript types, found this.
